title: Director, Volume Licensing Programs Modernization
description:
Overview
About Monetization Strategy & Licensing (MSL)
Monetization Strategy & Licensing (MSL) is a newly formed organization at the core of Microsoft's Business strategy. MSL brings together the teams that decide how Microsoft prices, packages, and monetizes its commercial products, together with the licensing programs and partner agreements that carry that commercial model to market.
The organization was established as Microsoft enters its next phase of AI-driven transformation, when customer expectations and commercial models are shifting faster than ever. MSL's charter is to modernize the commercial engine beneath that shift: evolving legacy licensing constructs toward cloud- and consumption-based models, growing multi-billion-dollar revenue streams, and keeping Microsoft's programs both compliant and competitive across a complex global regulatory landscape.
Role Overview
The Director, Volume Licensing Programs Modernization leads the modernization of Microsoft's legacy Volume Licensing (VL) programs: the Microsoft Products & Services Agreement (MPSA), Select and Select Plus, and the Open family of programs (Open License, Open Value, and Open Value Subscription). These programs were designed for a perpetual-license, on-premises world. As customer needs shift to cloud and consumption, this role will shape how they evolve alongside Microsoft’s modern commerce motions.
This role owns the strategy to evolve these programs and guide customers and partners toward CSP, MCA-E, and Web Direct, while preserving revenue, protecting customers with legitimate perpetual-licensing needs, and minimizing disruption to partners and channels. The successful candidate will operate with significant independence, lead complex cross-group work as an individual contributor, influencing without direct authority across finance, commerce, engineering, CELA, partner, and field teams, and bring well-framed, data-driven options to senior leadership.
Responsibilities
Strategic Programs You Will Modernize / Key Responsibilities
This role modernizes a set of long-lived, high-revenue programs that are central to Microsoft's shift toward subscription and cloud-based commerce:
Legacy VL Program Strategy and Roadmap
Own the end-to-end strategy for MPSA, Select / Select Plus, and Open Value / Open Value Subscription. title: AI Deployment Manager - Builder (Spanish- and Portuguese-Speaking)
description:
About the Team

The AI Deployment Manager (ADM) team enables organizations to turn OpenAI products into real, sustained impact through world-class enablement and training execution.

Our mission is to help customers successfully adopt and operationalize AI across their organizations. We partner with enterprises to translate the potential of OpenAI’s technology into durable capability—through structured training, technical enablement, and scalable deployment programs.

By helping customers move from experimentation to production, the ADM team accelerates time-to-value, deepens meaningful adoption, and helps make OpenAI indispensable to how organizations work.

About the Role

The AI Deployment Manager, Builder role is a specialist post-sales technical enablement role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. You will design and deliver technical learning experiences covering OpenAI APIs, Codex, agents, evaluations, and related platform capabilities. You will work with engineers, AI and platform teams, administrators, security stakeholders, product leaders, and executive sponsors.

This role blends deep technical fluency, instructional design, and customer advisory. You will lead live trainings, workshops, and adoption interventions for audiences ranging from hands-on builders to executive leaders, helping customers understand not just what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to use them effectively in real-world contexts.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence, increasing product adoption, helping customers progress toward production use, and turning lessons from individual engagements into resources and practices that benefit many customers.

This role is based in San Francisco or New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

In this role, you will:

 - Own the technical enablement of OpenAI products, including OpenAI APIs, Codex, Agents, Evaluations and other platform capabilities, helping define effective enablement patterns that support adoption across customer segments

 - Lead customer training and enablement across the full customer lifecycle, from initial onboarding through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.

 - Design and deliver high-impact training engagements, including onboarding sessions, advanced capability trainings, executive briefings, hackathons, and hands-on workshops for audiences ranging from senior leaders to working teams.

 - Drive customer activation, sustained usage, and measurable business value through structured enablement and deployment programs designed for durable adoption at scale

 - Partner closely with Sales, Solutions Architecture, and Product teams to define an effective enablement plan tailored to each customer’s use case, goals, and technical needs.

 - Partner closely with Sales, Solution Architects, Delivery Leads to drive adoption across our core product suite.

 - Develop and refine reusable training assets, playbooks, and best practices based on patterns observed across customers and regions.

 - Gather customer feedback from training and enablement engagements, synthesize themes across accounts, and relay insights to internal stakeholders to inform product and program improvements.

 - Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for designated product areas, building deep expertise, supporting internal enablement, identifying emerging customer use cases for new product surfaces, and aggregating customer feedback to inform product development.

You might thrive in this role if you:

 - Speak fluent business-level Spanish and Portuguese, as you will be engaging with Spanish and Portuguese speaking customers

 - Have 4+ years of experience in customer-facing or instructional roles, engaging C-level and senior technical audiences in complex enterprise environments.

 - Possess exceptional presentation and communication skills, particularly when conveying the value of technical concepts clearly to senior and executive-level audiences.

 - Strong technical depth across software engineering, the software development lifecycle, and APIs, with a practical understanding of how AI systems are built, evaluated, and operated in production, including RAG, evaluation strategies, agentic systems and key tradeoffs.

 - Proven experience leading structured technical trainings, such as API bootcamps, workshops, or enablement sessions, with the ability to design learning journeys, handle live questions, and reason through problems in real time.

 - Strong ability to connect technical features and capabilities to concrete business outcomes such as productivity, efficiency, cost reduction, risk mitigation, or revenue impact.

 - Have a humble attitude, an eagerness to help others, and a desire to pick up whatever knowledge you're missing to make both your team and our customers succeed.

 - Comfortable thinking on their feet in live customer settings, adapting quickly to new information, shifting priorities, and real-time questions while maintaining clarity, ownership, and momentum.

 - Are personally committed to fostering the safe and ethical evolution of AI.



About OpenAI

OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. 

We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic.

description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

The Growth team drives adoption and revenue for ChatGPT. This role focuses on B2B and small-business growth: helping business owners, functional leaders, and teams discover how ChatGPT can solve their work challenges and deliver value. We partner across product, engineering, product marketing, content, design, and analytics to turn customer insights and disciplined experimentation into sustainable growth.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We are seeking a growth marketer with deep expertise in search engine optimization (SEO) and a strong experimental approach to answer engine optimization (AEO) to grow ChatGPT adoption among small businesses. You will own the strategy and execution for reaching business buyers through organic search and AI-powered answers, connecting discovery to evaluation, workspace creation, and paid adoption.

You will build an organic acquisition program around how small businesses research problems, compare solutions, and choose tools for their teams. Your remit spans technical SEO, search and question research, content strategy, and AEO experimentation. You will partner with SMB Product Marketing and Content Marketing to translate business use cases, industry needs, and customer proof into useful discovery experiences, and with Web Growth to improve the path from organic discovery to conversion.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA or New York, NY. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the B2B / SMB SEO and AEO roadmap, prioritizing opportunities by business audience, use case, industry, buying intent, and potential contribution to customer acquisition and revenue.

 - Lead keyword, question, and audience research across the small-business buying journey—from identifying a business problem to comparing solutions and evaluating pricing, team adoption, and business requirements. Translate findings into prioritized content briefs and page opportunities.

 - Own the technical SEO roadmap with web and engineering partners, including crawlability, indexing, rendering, site architecture, internal linking, structured data, and migration readiness. Build durable foundations for discovering and understanding our business content.

 - Develop and test AEO approaches that help business buyers find accurate, useful information about ChatGPT in AI-powered search and answer experiences. Improve answer-focused content, product information, and supporting evidence; track visibility, citations, and referral quality while distinguishing observed results from hypotheses.

 - Partner with SMB Product Marketing and Content Marketing on use-case and industry pages, comparison and evaluation content, practical guides, and customer stories. Bring search insights and clear briefs; maintain accuracy, originality, and usefulness as the program scales.

 - Build measurement with Analytics that connects organic discovery to qualified business traffic, workspace creation, activation, paid conversion, and revenue. Segment performance by intent, audience, and market, and use experiments and cohort analysis to assess impact and attribution limits.

 - Partner with Web Growth, Design, and Product on landing-page and conversion experiments that help business visitors take the right next step. Align messaging, proof points, calls to action, and onward journeys with buyer intent, then evaluate downstream customer quality.

 - Build AI-assisted workflows for research, briefing, content refreshes, technical audits, and reporting, with human review and quality controls. Use programmatic approaches where they create distinct value for business audiences.

 - Coordinate execution across engineering, product marketing, content, web, and analytics partners. Establish a regular testing and learning cadence, and partner on localization to expand proven SEO and AEO approaches into priority markets.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - 10+ years in SEO or growth marketing, with a track record of growing qualified organic acquisition for B2B software or products serving small businesses. Experience with self-serve or product-led business acquisition is especially relevant.

 - Deep technical SEO expertise, including site architecture, crawling and indexing, structured data, migrations, and internal linking, combined with strong judgment about search intent and content quality.

 - Hands-on experience testing visibility in AI-powered search and answer experiences. You can design an AEO measurement approach, evaluate citations and referrals, and explain what the evidence does—and does not—show.

 - A strong understanding of small-business buyers and how their needs vary by role, company size, and industry. You can turn customer problems, solution comparisons, and buying questions into a focused organic growth strategy.

 - Strong collaboration with product marketing, content, engineering, design, web growth, and analytics teams. You can turn insights into clear briefs, prioritize shared roadmaps, and take initiatives through launch and iteration.

 - Strong analytical and experimentation skills, including search and web analytics, funnel and cohort analysis, and landing-page testing. You connect traffic and visibility to activation, paid adoption, and revenue rather than optimizing for rankings alone.

 - Hands-on experience publishing, refreshing, and measuring content through a CMS, including landing pages, reusable templates, and localized experiences. You are comfortable moving between strategic planning, technical audits, and page-level QA.

 - Experience using AI-assisted workflows and programmatic SEO to improve execution while preserving factual accuracy, original value, and a high-quality customer experience.

 - A test-and-learn mindset, clear communication, and comfort operating in a fast-changing environment. You balance curiosity about new discovery channels with disciplined prioritization and measurement.

description:
ABOUT THIS TEAM

The HR Business Partner (HRBP) team at OpenAI partners with leaders on complex organizational and talent decisions where the right path is not always obvious. We stay close enough to the business to understand how it works and focus our time on the decisions that benefit most from our judgment, context, and influence.

We work with urgency, empathy, and sound judgment. We value sincerity, intellectual honesty, and collaboration over ego.


ABOUT THIS ROLE

As a Senior HR Business Partner supporting Tech, you’ll partner with leaders in engineering, product, and other technical teams as they build and scale their organizations. You’ll get close enough to the work to understand what’s slowing teams down, then help leaders make decisions about structure, talent, and how teams work together as technical priorities evolve.

This is an individual contributor role reporting to an HRBP Lead. You’ll advise senior leaders on complex decisions and work directly with managers to make those decisions stick.


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Translate technical priorities into org and talent decisions. Help leaders decide what capabilities to build, how to structure teams, and where ownership needs to sit.

 - Diagnose what’s getting in the way of team performance. Use data and input from the people doing the work to separate structural issues from problems with roles, priorities, or how teams work together.

 - Develop technical leaders. Coach managers through performance, growth, and succession decisions, and help them set clear expectations for both people managers and individual contributors.

 - Lead change as technical priorities shift. Help leaders think through the impact of reorganizations or changes in ownership and communicate decisions clearly to the teams affected.

 - Build People practices that work for technical teams. Partner with fellow HRBPs and People specialists to adapt performance, development, and talent processes without adding unnecessary overhead.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU HAVE:

 - 7–10+ years of HR experience, including at least 5 years as an HR Business Partner in a high-growth or complex environment.

 - Experience partnering with engineering, product, or other technical organizations, and curiosity about how technical teams make decisions and deliver work.

 - A track record of helping technical leaders navigate org design, workforce planning, or talent decisions as teams grow or priorities change.

 - Skill in coaching senior leaders and managers, including the ability to challenge a decision constructively and maintain trust.

 - Sound judgment under pressure and the ability to act on incomplete information while staying open to new evidence.

 - Discretion, fairness, and sound judgment when the stakes are high.

This role is based in our San Francisco or New York office and is not available remotely. We offer relocation support to new employees. Our hybrid model is three days in the office per week, with optional work from home on Thursdays and Fridays.

title: Software Engineer, Presence
description:
ABOUT THE TEAM

Presence is OpenAI’s team building AI agents that organizations can trust to handle real conversations and get things done. Our mission is to turn advances in frontier models into dependable systems that can resolve customer issues, support employees, and improve through experience in production.

Imagine calling about an unexpected charge. An agent needs to understand your situation, verify your identity, find the relevant account information, apply the right policy, and resolve the issue or bring in a person. It needs to do all of this naturally, accurately, and quickly, even when the conversation takes an unexpected turn. Presence brings together the models, execution systems, integrations, and controls that make experiences like this possible across voice, chat and email.

One of our most exciting challenges is what happens after an agent goes live. We're building a system for understanding where agents fail and making them better: investigate a production conversation, reproduce the problem in an evaluation, use Codex to develop a fix, test it against the current agent, and measure the result after deployment. Our ambition is to make more of this improvement process agentic over time, while giving people control over what changes reach users.

Read the launch announcement https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/.

 


WHAT WE WORK ON

 - Realtime voice: Natural conversations with fast responses, interruptions, and reliable audio, even under heavy traffic.

 - Agent systems: Orchestration, reasoning, tool execution, integrations with company systems, and enforcing permissions and policies.

 - Agent quality: Production debugging, simulations, evaluation infrastructure, regression testing, and measuring whether changes improve real outcomes.

 - Product and developer experience: Making it easier for teams to build, test, deploy, and operate sophisticated agents using Codex and OpenAI's capabilities.

 


IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

You'll work at the intersection of frontier research, product engineering, and production systems, with a direct feedback loop from people using what you build. We collaborate closely with Research, Forward Deployed Engineers, and customers to understand where models and systems break down and turn those lessons into improvements that can benefit many deployments.

The impact is already tangible. At launch, Presence was resolving 75% of issues coming into OpenAI's English phone support without a human, and its Codex-assisted improvement process helped cut transfers to people by 15 percentage points over ten days. Introducing OpenAI Presence https://openai.com/index/introducing-openai-presence/

We're looking for people excited by ambitious engineering problems, building products people depend on, and helping define how AI agents are developed and improved in the real world.

 


YOUR BACKGROUND MIGHT LOOK SOMETHING LIKE:

 - 9+ years of professional engineering experience, excluding internships, in backend, platform, or product engineering roles.

 - A track record of hands-on technical leadership, including setting architecture, breaking complex problems into clear implementation plans, and guiding engineers through delivery.

 - Deep backend engineering and systems design skills, with proficiency in at least one backend programming language and experience designing services, data models, and interfaces that remain reliable as usage grows.

 - End-to-end ownership of complex systems or product capabilities, from ambiguous requirements and technical design through implementation, launch, and production iteration.

 - Strong production engineering judgment: you can diagnose difficult failures, reason about performance and scalability, and improve reliability through testing, observability, and operational discipline.

 - Strong product judgment that connects technical decisions to user needs, with the ability to balance delivery speed, reliability, security, and long-term maintainability.

 - The ability to move between backend infrastructure and product experiences, contribute across the stack when needed, and quickly learn unfamiliar systems, tools, and domains.

 - Clear technical communication and effective collaboration across disciplines, including explaining trade-offs, creating alignment, and driving complex work forward while remaining hands-on.

You will partner with Hardware Engineering, Quality, Product, Finance, and Data Engineering to build the governed hardware data foundation.
What You Will Do:
Hardware KPI Ownership
Own the analytics layer for the hardware portfolio scorecard—partner with Hardware Engineering, Product, Quality, and Finance to define, document, and deliver the KPIs that show up in board and external reporting (including but not limited to activation rate, warranty rate, return/RMA rate, and defect/quality rate).
Establish each hardware KPI as a governed, audit-grade data product—locked definitions, single owner, data build tool (dbt) tests, full lineage from source systems, formal sign-off, and a documented change-management process.
Build and own the hardware data products.
Be the analytics representative in external audit cycles—produce documentation, walk auditors through lineage, and ensure controls and traceability are reflected in how hardware portfolio and quality metrics are produced.
Hardware Quality & Portfolio Performance Analytics
Partner closely with Hardware Engineering and Firmware teams on product quality data—defect rates, failure modes, warranty claims, RMA root cause, and field reliability by product generation, SKU, and manufacturing batch.
Deliver hardware portfolio performance analytics—sell-through, activation, and retention by product generation and SKU—that give Hardware leadership a single trusted view of what's working and what isn't.
Drive adoption of self-service reporting by Hardware Engineering, Quality, and Product partners using a variety of analytics tools and creating clear documentation to reduce one-off reporting and free up analyst time for analysis.
Platform Migration & Data Engineering
Migrate hardware portfolio and quality reporting from legacy stacks (Snowflake + Tableau + Sheets) to our Databricks-based platform, with dbt-modeled metrics, Unity Catalog lineage, and Databricks SQL / Genie as the executive-facing surface.
Coordinate with source-system owners across manufacturing, quality systems, and e-commerce (NetSuite, contract-manufacturer feeds, Zuora) and the Data Engineering team to ensure clean ingestion, correct dimensional modeling, and clear lineage from factory output through to sell-through, activation, and quality events.
Resolve systems data quality issues to ensure that reporting is trustworthy end to end.
Build and maintain the Hardware domain's data products in Databricks, mentoring analysts on dimensional modeling, dbt practices, and the Golden Path for publishing governed metrics for reporting and for MCP/agentic AI consumption.
Tooling & Innovation
Continuously evaluate emerging tools (Unity Catalog, Databricks Genie, AI-assisted SQL/modeling via Cursor and Claude Code, semantic-layer technologies) to improve productivity and accuracy in hardware portfolio and quality reporting.
We have offices in San Francisco, San Diego and Los Angeles for those who prefer hybrid or office settings. ŌURA employees in other major cities (like Boston and New York) occasionally gather informally at local co-working locations.
What you'll bring:
7+ years in analytics, business intelligence, or a related data-focused role, with at least 3+ years specifically supporting Hardware, Product Quality, or Manufacturing.
Demonstrated experience building executive-level reporting for a physical-product business that is trusted by leadership and survives external scrutiny (Board, auditors, investors).
Deep working knowledge of hardware data domains: BOM and component costing, warranty and RMA/returns, defect and quality rates, manufacturing yield, and how transactional systems (ERP, contract-manufacturer feeds, hardware use platforms) flow into reported numbers.
Expert in SQL with experience writing complex queries for operational and financial data extraction, reconciliation, and modeling.
Expertise in dimensional modeling for hardware and quality reporting (conformed dimensions across SKU, product generation, channel, geo; slowly-changing dimensions for product and cost hierarchies; period-over-period comparisons).
Experience with dbt—including tests, documentation, exposures, and contracts.
Experience with Databricks strongly preferred (Unity Catalog, Databricks SQL, Lakeflow, Genie); deep Snowflake experience acceptable with willingness to migrate.
Experience with modern BI tools (Tableau, Looker, Databricks SQL Dashboards, Power BI) and a clear point of view on when each is the right fit.
Track record of working alongside external auditors (PwC, Deloitte, EY, KPMG) and building documentation that withstands audit review.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills—able to brief a hardware or finance leader on a number, then explain to an analyst how the data behind it works.
Thrive in a fast-paced, highly collaborative global work environment that spans engineering, quality, and offices across time zones.
Nice to have:
What Makes You Stand Out • Familiarity with adjacent tooling and sources: AWS, GitHub, NetSuite/ERP, Fivetran, Python, semantic layers, quality management systems (QMS), and contract-manufacturer (CM) data integrations.
Experience standing up a hardware data contract and product/SKU dimension (dim_hardware) from scratch in a high-growth consumer hardware company.
Experience building governed KPI programs through a formal external audit (e.g., PwC, Big 4), including COGS, quality, and units-sold reconciliation.

title: Staff Engineer
description:
ABOUT QUINCE
Quince is a destination for builders, creators, innovators, and operators who want to come together and challenge the status quo. Our mission is simple: make really high quality essentials for really low prices, fairly and sustainably. We deliver on that mission through a unique manufacturer-to-consumer (M2C) model eliminating the layers of traditional retail that add cost and result in consumers paying more than they need to. We find, build relationships with, and work directly with the manufacturing partners behind some of the world’s finest products. From there, our teams design smart, efficient operational processes  and build and deploy proprietary technology, AI, and analytics to help us scale fast.
What began with a small assortment of elevated basics has quickly grown into a cross-category brand spanning apparel, accessories, home goods, and more. Today, tens of millions of people across a growing number of countries come – and return – to Quince because they trust us to deliver.
OUR CULTURE
Quince is a culture built for builders by builders. Our way of working starts with a blank sheet of paper. We question conventional thinking, use technology and data to uncover new opportunities, and move quickly to turn ideas into reality. We aren’t interested in replicating how others do retail. We’re building a better way – at a speed and scale unlike anything that’s been done before.
We dream big and chase the hard problems others shy away from. Rejecting long-held assumptions is part of our company's DNA.  Where conventional wisdom says you have to choose – soft or durable, speed or rigor, quality or price – we ask why that trade-off has to exist in the first place.
Our pace is fast and the bar is high because our customers expect a lot from us and we refuse to let them down. We believe the best results come from challenging ourselves, learning from one another, and building on each other's strengths.
Here, responsibility is not determined by role, tenure, or seniority. Every team member - no matter their level - has the opportunity to drive our business and shape our trajectory.
If you’re someone who likes to imagine new possibilities and build better systems rather than plug-in to outdated ones, Quince is the place for you.
Hiring is one of the highest-leverage systems at a company scaling as fast as Quince, and today it runs on stitched-together vendor tools that were never designed for our volume, our bar, or our operating speed. Role Summary This position is for a Service Advisor, the central point of contact and trusted guide for our owners throughout their service experience. This role requires a deeply empathetic, organized, and brand-focused individual who thrives on creating positive interactions and seamless processes. The Service Advisor is a critical liaison, translating complex vehicle needs into clear, confidence-inspiring communication for our customers, while coordinating flawlessly with the service production team. This job description outlines the full spectrum of skills required, and candidates will be assessed against this spectrum to determine the appropriate level for their expertise, from entry-level to senior advisor. This is a level-agnostic posting designed to recruit Service Advisor candidates across various seniority levels in the organization; specific level availability fluctuates and is determined by current business needs. The shift for this position is Monday through Friday, 12pm-9pm. This position comes with a 15% pay differential that occurs between 6pm - 9pm Responsibilities Serve as the primary point of contact for owners, managing the service experience from initial appointment scheduling to vehicle handover. Listen actively to understand owner concerns, accurately document them in the repair order, and set clear expectations for the visit. Translate technical information from technicians into simple, understandable language for owners. Proactively communicate updates on vehicle status, managing timelines and ensuring a transparent process. Coordinate with the Parts and Production teams to ensure all aspects of the service visit are aligned. Prepare and explain estimates and invoices with clarity and accuracy. Ensure every owner leaves feeling cared for, confident in the work performed, and more connected to the Rivian brand. Manage internal systems to maintain impeccable records of all customer communications and repairs, ensuring all performance metrics are met or exceeded. Uphold Rivian's standards for hospitality, presentation, and process in every interaction. Act as the on-site liaison between Rivian’s centralized Service Support Operations Center and local Service Center operations. Support the launch and setup of new Service Center locations, training initiatives, and process improvements. Assist in warranty repairs and ensure compliance with state and federal automotive repair laws. Manage relationships with third-party vendors, documenting work orders and coordinating with production team to ensure seamless after-hours service completion. This role may require regular interaction with customers and their families, 3rd party affiliates, and suppliers within Rivian facilities, on mobile service routes, or at community outreach events. Qualifications General Requirements: High School Diploma or GED is preferred Must be at least 21 years old. Must possess a valid driver’s license and maintain a clean driving record. Must be available for a 40-hour work week, which may include weekends, holidays, and varied shifts based on business needs. Proficient with laptops, computers, and modern software suites (Windows, Google Workspace, Mac, CRM systems, etc.). Exceptional organizational skills, a meticulous attention to detail, and a passion for creating order. Outstanding written and verbal communication skills in English. Ability to perform physical tasks such as lifting up to 50 lbs., sitting, standing, walking, and frequent use of hands for grasping tools and data entry. Physical exertion may be required to perform occupational tasks (sitting, standing, walking, bending, kneeling, carrying, reaching, pushing, pulling, and lifting up to 50 lbs.). Ability to read and speak fluent English. Ability to see, read and interpret documents such as governmental regulations, safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions or schematics. Experience: Experience in a customer-facing role is required. Backgrounds in hospitality, retail, or fast-paced, system-driven restaurants are highly valued. Automotive service experience is a plus but not a prerequisite for entry-level roles. Proven ability to de-escalate sensitive situations and resolve customer concerns with empathy and professionalism. Experience managing complex scheduling, billing, and work order systems is a plus. Spectrum of Advisor Skills Customer Engagement & Hospitality: An advisor must be the face of Rivian service. Foundational skills include a warm, professional demeanor and the ability to follow established communication guidelines. An advanced advisor moves beyond guidelines to provide anticipatory service, remembering owner preferences, proactively addressing unstated needs, and building genuine, long-term relationships that foster trust and brand loyalty. Technical Acumen & Translation: A core competency is the ability to bridge the communication gap between the technician and the owner. A developing advisor can accurately transcribe customer concerns and look up vehicle information. A highly skilled advisor comprehends complex diagnostic concepts, asks clarifying questions of technicians, and can then translate that information into simple, clear, and confident explanations for the owner, ensuring they feel informed and empowered, never confused or intimidated. Process & Systems Management: The service experience relies on operational precision. An entry-level advisor manages the entire service workflow, from booking appointments to closing out work orders. An expert advisor masters this workflow, handling a high volume of complex work orders simultaneously, coordinating seamlessly with parts and production, and identifying process inefficiencies to ensure the entire front-of-house operation runs with impeccable rhythm and consistency. Problem Resolution & De-escalation: Service can be stressful for owners, and advisors must be a calming, confident presence. Join Our Team as an Electrical Engineer Engineer III!
Are you passionate about Electrical Engineering?   S&C Electric Company is seeking a dynamic individual to join our Fuses and Circuit Switchers function. As an Electrical Engineer III, you’ll be crucial in ensuring smooth operations and supporting our diverse team.
The Electrical Engineer III demonstrates strong technical expertise, initiative, and leadership in electrical design and cross-functional collaboration. They contribute to larger, more complex projects, engage with internal and external teams, and begin influencing departmental and organizational goals. They are expected to work independently, mentor junior engineers, and help shape the future of the department through innovation and strategic thinking.
Key Responsibilities:
Research & Technology: Conduct independent electromechanical testing and analyze results. Document findings and report insights to support design decisions and inform product improvements. Attend conferences and stay current with industry trends. Identify opportunities to apply emerging technologies and practices to advance departmental capabilities and product innovation.
Product Support: Drive sustaining engineering projects, including novel designs and first-time implementations. Execute tasks, identify next steps, and ensure successful execution from concept through completion. Serve as a go-to resource for solving complex problems with products currently in production, and RMA testing and analysis.
Design & Application: Design new electrical components and systems, perform calculations, and apply practical engineering knowledge to real-world challenges. Demonstrate a strong understanding of mechanical processes and integration.
New Product Design: Design and development of innovative electrical components and systems for testing, product development, ensuring manufacturability, performance, and cost-effectiveness. Assist in the process from concept through prototyping and production readiness while collaborating with cross-functional teams to integrate electrical solutions seamlessly.
Technical Mentorship: Mentor and guide more junior engineers, provide technical guidance, and drive brainstorming sessions. Act as the go-to resource for resolving design and component-related issues.
Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work with internal teams across departments and engage with external partners, including international groups. Build relationships and contribute to broader organizational initiatives.
Strategic Contribution: Support institutional goals by contributing to process improvements, technical strategy, and departmental growth. Help shape how the team fits into the broader industry landscape.

Attend in-person or virtual meetings as requested or required.
Communicate effectively and respectfully with others.
Other responsibilities as assigned

Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Physics or a related field.
5-7 Years of experience in Electrical or Electronics Engineering.
Great understanding of electrical circuit design and programming.
Good skills in effective problem-solving and able to communicate verbally and via documentation across some levels of the organization related to concepts of supply-chain, production, electronics and problem-solving.
A great understanding of various manufacturing technologies and methods, preferably within the electronics manufacturing industry but also with mechanical parts and assemblies.
Good interpersonal skills to establish meaningful relationships built on mutual trust and respect, and foster collaborative working relationships amongst a diverse audience.
Great communication skills (written, verbal, listening, and presentation), able to partner with and communicate with customers, both technical and non-technical verbally and via summarized data analysis and solid documentation.
Commitment to fostering a culture of continuous improvement and innovation within the quality function.
Good organizational planning, coordinating internal and external resources, and juggling key demands.
Sound business sense and analytical skills with the ability to use, analyze and present data that supports conclusions and drives informed actions to resolve complex problems and drive learning.
Ability to work in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines, including the flexibility to work extended hours when necessary.
Great computer skills and ability to use Microsoft Office applications, specifically Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Project, and Power BI, or other similar systems. Including great data analysis and documentation skills.

Samsara's Data Science, ML, and Data Platform team brings together data science, production ML, data engineering, and data platform to turn emerging AI capabilities into reliable products. These products help customers run safer, more efficient physical operations. Define an AI-native strategy and rethink the roadmap from first principles as capabilities change. Choose what to build, buy, stop, and scale.
Partner with Product and Engineering to take intelligence from experiment to deployment, adoption, and continuous improvement in customer experiences.
Build a trusted data foundation by making certified metrics, discoverable metadata, and traceable outputs available to people and agents across the organization, within clear permissions.

Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices
Hire, develop and lead an inclusive, engaged, and high performing team

Experience leading scientists and engineers through managers, holding a high technical bar outside your own specialty, and changing how teams work

Experience with agentic analytics: building investigation workflows over enterprise data

Experience running large-scale data or ML platforms with demanding reliability, cost, and governance requirements

This role contributes to Starbucks’ success by safeguarding information and systems assets against unauthorized use, disclosure, modification, damage, or loss. The director is the accountable owner of the Data Protection domain, translating enterprise risk priorities, regulatory expectations, and business needs into clear objectives, investment choices, and accountable roadmaps, while bringing evidence-based recommendations to the ciso and executive leaders. title: Deal Pricing
description:
Deal Pricing
About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow revenue, and pursue new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a significant amount of work ahead. This creates an unprecedented opportunity to help expand access to the global economy while doing some of the most important work of your career.
About the Team
Deal Pricing is a dedicated global function that provides pricing expertise, financial insights, and deal support for negotiated users across Stripe’s global Go-to-Market (GTM) organization. We help ensure that deals create sustainable economic value for Stripe by establishing commercial frameworks for a scaling sales organization, actively supporting large and strategic opportunities, and delivering pricing insights and recommendations to Sales, Finance, Product, and other cross-functional leaders.
What You’ll Do
You will develop and improve pricing tools used by GTM, Renewals, Deal Pricing, and other teams to evaluate deal economics and support commercial decision-making. Depending on the business need, you may define requirements for systems teams or build offline tools in Google Sheets from the ground up. You will also develop and review pricing dashboards, translate data into actionable insights, and provide recommendations to senior leadership.
Responsibilities
Collaborate with Engineering, Product Management, GTM, and Pricing Strategy teams to evaluate pricing strategies, define and test requirements, and support Stripe’s Quote-to-Cash systems.
Plan and execute user acceptance testing (UAT) to ensure that system tools meet business requirements and quality standards.
Build financial models and tools to evaluate the deal economics of Stripe’s payments and software portfolio.
Analyze financial and commercial data to identify trends, opportunities, and risks within Stripe’s pricing strategies.
Manage and triage tooling questions, enhancement requests, and bug reports, ensuring issues are prioritized and resolved effectively.
Define key business metrics and KPIs to assess business health, proactively highlighting emerging risks and opportunities.
Build and maintain dashboards that deliver clear, decision-ready business insights.
Apply and develop AI-enabled tools to improve efficiency and scale workflows across GBS.
Who You Are
We’re looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements below. If you meet these qualifications, we encourage you to apply. Preferred qualifications are helpful but not required.
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.
5+ years of financial modeling experience, preferably within fintech, SaaS, banking, or a related industry.
Proficiency with data analysis tools, including SQL and Google Sheets or Microsoft Excel.
Strong quantitative and analytical skills, with exceptional attention to detail.
A finance-oriented mindset and strong operational discipline, with the ability to build scalable, repeatable processes and systems.
Demonstrated ability to establish collaborative relationships with cross-functional business partners and executives.
Strong problem-solving and critical-thinking skills.
Effective written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex data clearly to varied audiences.
Ability to navigate ambiguity and thrive in an unstructured, fast-paced environment.
Active use of AI tools to improve productivity and scale impact.
Preferred Qualifications
Programming or automation experience with JavaScript and Salesforce.
Familiarity with financial metrics, pricing strategies, and commercial deal structures.
Understanding of database concepts and data manipulation techniques.
Experience partnering with Sales, Engineering, Product Management, and other cross-functional teams.
Experience developing dashboards and interactive reporting solutions.

About Stripe
Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Create written analyses, documents and presentations including but not limited to: project initiation documentation, market reports, RFPs, proposal comparison spreadsheets, letters of intent

Experience working for both in-house real estate teams for tenant end-user and external service provider

title: Technical Operations Engineer, Revenue
description:
Who we are

About the team
Stripe’s infrastructure powers businesses all over the world. We process payments, run marketplaces, detect fraud, help entrepreneurs start an internet business from anywhere in the world, build world-class developer-friendly APIs, and more. Revenue Foundations provides a central entry point for Stripe products to monetize in global markets. It is ultimately responsible for the systems, programs, and operations that generate Stripe’s revenue and the economic models we have with our customers. This is accomplished through a sophisticated pricing onboarding tooling and workflow management, unified billing engine, and custom solutions for our largest enterprise users.
Our work is core to Stripe’s business. We sit at the intersection of product, sales, engineering, finance, and operations, acting as the connective tissue that ensures users have a frictionless billing experience with Stripe.
What you’ll do
Every record in our data warehouse is vitally important for the businesses that use Stripe, so we’re looking for people with a strong background in business and analytics to help us scale while maintaining correct and complete data. You’ll be working with a variety of internal teams across Sales, Engineering, Finance, Product, and Accounting to ensure data completeness, billing reliability, and build product requirements. description:

Our platform serves as the technology backbone for modern transit networks, transforming antiquated and Via is on a mission to create public transportation systems that provide greater access to jobs, healthcare, and education. With hundreds of agency partners around the world, Via is recognized as the leading transportation technology and service provider globally.
As a Class A Mechanic  on Via's Operations team, you'll be hands-on every day - diagnosing, repairing, and maintaining the buses and support vehicles that keep our transit service running. This is a technical, floor-focused role for someone who takes pride in getting under the hood, solving problems the right way the first time, and keeping a fleet on the road safely and reliably.
This is an in-person position with the expectation that you will be on-site 5 days per week. While standard schedules are provided, this role does require flexibility to work occasional evenings, Saturdays, and extended hours as business needs arise.
What You'll Do:
Perform routine preventive maintenance on electric vehicles & transit vehicles, and support equipment, including fluid changes, filter replacements, brake inspections, tire rotations, and scheduled service intervals
Diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic issues across engines, transmissions, braking systems, HVAC, suspension, steering, and electrical systems.
Conduct pre-trip, post-trip, and DOT-compliant safety inspections, identifying defects and completing repairs in line with regulatory and manufacturer standards.
Respond to road calls and in-service breakdowns, troubleshooting issues on-site and coordinating with the Maintenance Manager to minimize service disruption.
Use automotive test equipment, diagnostic software, and manufacturer diagrams to isolate issues and verify repairs.
Complete accurate work orders and maintain detailed service records for each vehicle, including labor, parts used, and root-cause notes.
Keep the shop and work areas clean, organized, and safe: tools returned, fluids stored properly, and hazards addressed before they become issues.
Who You Are:
Vocational automotive training and hands-on experience in medium/heavy-duty vehicle maintenance (minimum 2 years preferred; EVs, transit bus, or diesel experience a plus).
Hands-on problem solver who enjoys working on the floor, not behind a desk.
Comfortable reading schematics, wiring diagrams, and technical manuals.
Proficient with diagnostic tools and comfortable learning new maintenance software.
Detail-oriented with documentation - work orders are closed out cleanly, records are accurate, and the next shift knows exactly what happened.
Comfortable with physical work, including lifting, bending, standing for extended periods, and working in varied shop conditions.
Licenses and Certification Requirements:
Hold a valid driver's license.
Hold a high school diploma or GED certificate.
Six ASE Transit Certifications mandatory (Medium/Heavy Truck or Transit Bus series — e.g., H-series or T-series).
CDL Class B with Passenger endorsement a plus (or willingness to obtain within a defined period post-hire).
At least 21 years old.
Successful completion of mandatory pre-employment drug test, criminal background check, and motor vehicle records check.
Pass a drug screening and background check: no felonies, clean MVR, no DUI/DWI or reckless driving convictions, and no more than 2 speeding tickets.
Able to pass a pre-employment physical.

Final salary will be determined by the candidate's experience, knowledge, and skills. Salary reflected does not include equity or variable pay, where applicable.

We are proud to offer a generous and comprehensive benefits package for full-time employees, including health and retirement benefits.
